Subjective:
- Identity: Name Jack Smith; Date of birth October 31, 1990.
- Presenting complaint: Left-ear hearing loss for about six weeks; associated left-ear tinnitus; intermittent dizziness.
- History:
  - Prior brief episode of hearing issue about a year ago (lasted a couple of days).
  - In the six-week period, left ear symptoms are on-and-off; tinnitus can be triggered or relieved by watching TV or listening to music.
  - No ear pain, no discharge, no fever reported.
  - Right ear hearing reportedly normal.
- Medications: None mentioned.
- Allergies: None mentioned.
- Social history: Not documented.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed yet (plan to assess in clinic).
- Symptoms reported by patient:
  - Left ear hearing loss.
  - Left ear tinnitus.
  - Intermittent dizziness described as off-balance, not associated with nausea or spinning.
- Other: No fever, no chest pain or palpitations.
- Right ear: Hearing described as normal by patient.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left ear hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent dizziness:
   - Assessment: Unilateral left-ear hearing loss with tinnitus; intermittent dizziness.
   - Differential: Cerumen impaction (wax blockage) suspected; other etiologies to be considered after ear examination.
   - Investigations planned: Otoscopic/ear examination by a GP within 4–5 days to assess for blockage and tympanic membrane status.
   - Treatment planned: Schedule face-to-face ear exam; refrain from using cotton buds; provide tinnitus information leaflet link to read prior to appointment.
   - Referrals: None at this time; will be seen by another GP with notes from this visit.

2. Tinnitus:
   - Assessment: Tinnitus present; acknowledged as a condition with limited fully understood etiology.
   - Investigations planned: Provide link to tinnitus leaflet for patient education.
   - Treatment planned: Patient education about tinnitus and potential management options; next steps contingent on ear examination results.
   - Referrals: None at this time.
